login.welcome: Welcome! Your exciting journey into the realm of Vision AI Platform starts right here. Let reCamera redefine your vision of possibilities.
login.agreeSuffix: . By checking the box, users understand reCamera operates solely on local networks and commit to maintaining enterprise-grade network security for all vision AI operations.
login.oldPasswordExtraPrefix: For first time login, default password is
login.newPasswordExtra: Password must be 8-32 characters and include letters, numbers, and symbols
login.passwordMismatch: The new password that you entered do not match!

agreement.intro: Welcome to reCamera Vision AI System. To ensure secure operation of your AI-powered camera, please review and confirm:
agreement.localIntro: This vision AI camera functions exclusively within local networks. You agree:
agreement.local1: Not to configure external/remote access capabilities
agreement.local2: To maintain all connections within your private network environment
agreement.local3: To disable UPnP/WAN exposure features if present
agreement.netIntro: By proceeding, you confirm that your network:
agreement.net4: Uses strong unique credentials (recommended 12+ character password)
agreement.dataIntro: As a vision AI camera, reCamera:
agreement.data1: Processes video data locally unless otherwise specified
agreement.data3: Excludes cloud connectivity by default design
agreement.respIntro: You acknowledge that Seeed Studio is not liable for:
agreement.resp1: Security incidents from unsecured network environments
agreement.resp3: Performance issues when used beyond local network parameters

loading.waiting: Please wait for node-red service to get start, it takes around 1 and an half minutes.
loading.errorBefore: Looks like something went wrong with system. Please check system and restart, or contact

apps.title: Applications
apps.subtitle: Each application is a complete scene solution. Only one application can hold the camera at a time.
apps.loadError: Could not load the application list. The appMgr service may be unavailable on this firmware.
apps.noAppsHint: Deploy one from the SenseCraft App, or upload a solution package (.deb) with Install App.
apps.activateContent: Switching applications will stop the currently running application and interrupt its RTSP/MQTT output. The camera will be handed over to the new application.
apps.stopContent: The application and its streams will be stopped. You can activate it again at any time.

install.title: Install Application
install.hint: Upload an application package (.deb). Once installed, the application appears in the gallery automatically.
install.trust: Packages are installed with system privileges. Only install packages from sources you trust.
install.selectFile: Click or drag a .deb package here
install.badChars: The file name contains unsupported characters. Use only letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore or plus.
install.installing: Installing package (opkg)… this can take up to two minutes.
install.busy: Another app operation is in progress. Please try again in a moment.
install.success: Installation completed. The application list has been refreshed.
install.downloading: Downloading {{file}} … (fetched by your browser; the camera needs no internet)
install.catalogUnavailableHint: This computer cannot reach sensecraft-statics.seeed.cc right now. Use "Upload .deb" instead, or deploy from the SenseCraft App.
install.noSpace: Not enough storage: about {{need}} MB needed, {{free}} MB free. Remove an app or some model files first.

apps.hwMissingTooltip: This device is missing required hardware: {{list}}
apps.orphanTooltip: This app's init script is no longer on the device — only a leftover entry remains. Uninstall it and install again.

uninstall.title: Uninstall {{name}}?
uninstall.content: Removes the application and its config from the device. Model files are kept — other apps may share them. You can reinstall it at any time.

live.title: Live Debug
live.noActiveHint: Activate an application to view and debug its output.
live.debugStreamHint: Taps H.264 from the device only while enabled — zero overhead when off.
live.resultOverlayHint: Draw inference boxes over the video.
live.pipelineHint: This application runs a fixed multi-model pipeline — its components cannot be switched.
live.noMessages: No messages received yet — waiting for inference results.
live.enableDebugHint: Enable the debug stream to see live inference results here.
live.debugOffHint: Debug stream is off. Toggle it on to preview the camera in the browser.
live.fallbackDebugUnavailable: The debug stream is unavailable right now. You can still open the application's RTSP stream directly:
live.fallbackNoDebug: This application does not provide a browser debug stream. Open its RTSP stream with a player such as VLC:
live.fallbackNoRtsp: No RTSP address declared by this application.
live.vlcHint: VLC: Media → Open Network Stream → paste the address above.
live.switchModelContent: The application will restart to load the new model. Streams will be briefly interrupted.
live.modelUpdated: Model updated. The application is restarting with the new model.
live.gimbalPlaceholder: A gimbal (CAN motor bus) was detected on this device. Pan/tilt control from this page arrives in Phase 6.
live.privacyBlurHint: Conceals the people the camera detects. Device-wide, applied immediately, without interrupting the view. Full settings live on the Device page.
live.privacyBlurAlphaHint: 255 hides the subject completely; lower lets the picture through in proportion. Takes effect as soon as you release — judge it against the view above.

device.subtitle: Low-level device controls and health.
device.ledUnavailableMsg: LED "{{name}}" is not available on this device
device.noBattery: No battery detected on this device.
device.sensorUnavailable: Sensor endpoint unavailable on this firmware.
device.timezoneNotApplied: Time set, but timezone "{{tz}}" was not accepted by the device
device.ntpFailed: NTP sync failed — the device needs internet access
device.timeHint: "Sync from browser" copies this browser's clock and timezone to the device — works offline. NTP requires internet on the device.
device.powerHint: Both actions interrupt all running applications.
device.rebootContent: The device will restart. All running applications and streams will be interrupted.
device.shutdownContent: The device will power off. You will need physical access to turn it back on.

audio.silent: No sound detected (mic may be disconnected or too quiet)
audio.speaker: Speaker
audio.playConfirm: Test sound played — confirm you can hear it at the device
audio.playRecordingFailed: Failed to play recording — record first and check the speaker
audio.playHint: The test sound is a fixed tone; Play on device speaker plays back the clip you just recorded (verifies the mic + speaker loopback).
audio.busy: Audio device is busy — another operation is in progress
audio.micHint: Records from the on-board microphone (16 kHz mono) and plays it back in this browser. The test sound comes out of the device speaker.
audio.speakerOnlyHint: The test sound plays from the device speaker.

config.title: Configuration
config.saveContent: The new configuration will be saved to the device. If the application is running it will restart, briefly interrupting its streams.
config.savedRestarting: Configuration saved — the application is restarting.
config.busy: Another app operation is in progress — try again in a moment
config.zoneHint: Click to add vertices (max {{max}}), drag a vertex to move it. Double-click or press Done to finish.
config.zoneInvalid: Invalid area — it is too small or self-intersecting
config.lineTooShort: Line is too short — draw a longer line
config.lineHint: Click twice to place endpoints A and B, drag to adjust. The arrow marks the "in" direction.
config.gridHint: Debug stream is off — drawing on a blind grid. Enable the debug stream to calibrate on the live view.

validation.passwordPattern: Password must be 8 to 32 characters and include letters, numbers, and symbols.

network.disableConfirm: This action will prevent you from access this web dashboard. Are you sure want to turn off it now?
network.ipInvalid: Invalid IP configuration. Check the IP address, prefix length (1-32), gateway and DNS fields.
network.ipConfirmContent: If you are changing the network interface you are currently using to access this device, you will need to reconnect using the new address after saving. The USB direct connection address 192.168.42.1 always remains available as a recovery channel.

security.noKeys: There are no SSH keys associated with your device.
security.passwordExtra: Password must be 8-32 characters and include letters, numbers, and symbols
security.removeConfirm: This action cannot revert, are you sure you want to remove this SSH key?

runtimeMode.title: Runtime Mode
runtimeMode.consoleDesc: Production mode: the C++ application gallery owns the camera. Node-RED and sscma-node stay disabled.
runtimeMode.noderedDesc: Graphical flow editor for prototyping and debugging (lower performance). Console applications are stopped.
runtimeMode.confirmContent: This stops the currently running application/flows and hands the camera over to the other mode. The switch takes up to a minute; the page will reload automatically when it completes.
runtimeMode.busy: A mode switch is already in progress, please wait
runtimeMode.failed: Failed to switch the runtime mode
runtimeMode.noderedBanner: The device is running in Node-RED mode — console applications are stopped and unavailable.
runtimeMode.actionUnavailable: Not available in Node-RED mode. Switch back to Console mode first.
runtimeMode.forceConsoleDesc: Emergency recovery: if Node-RED mode stops responding, forcibly kill its services and return to Console mode.
runtimeMode.forceConsoleConfirmContent: This immediately kills Node-RED / sscma-node (no graceful shutdown) and returns to Console mode, and drops a backstop flag so the next reboot also returns to Console. Use only when the device is stuck in Node-RED mode and cannot switch back normally. The page will reload when it completes.

system.rebootHint: Please reboot the device to finish the update
system.updatingHint: The update can last several minutes depends on the network condition
system.rebootingContent: Please refresh the page in 5 seconds

camera.restarted: The running application was restarted to apply them.
camera.busy: Another operation is in progress, please retry shortly
camera.hint: Saving restarts the running application to apply the changes (the debug stream will briefly drop).
camera.liveHint: Saving restarts the running application to apply the changes (the debug stream will briefly drop).

focus.title: Focus Assist
focus.enableHint: Poll the camera's live sharpness score once per second — turn the lens until the bar peaks.
focus.hint: The score is relative — adjust the lens for the highest value. The dark marker is the best score seen this session.

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.subtitle: A web shell on the device itself — full command-line access without SSH.

ha.title: Home Assistant
ha.subtitle: Publish detection events to Home Assistant over MQTT and view the camera stream in your dashboard.
ha.noderedNotice: The device is in Node-RED mode. The HA integration is provided by the Console application — settings saved here take effect after switching back to Console mode.
ha.passwordUnchanged: Leave empty to keep the current password
ha.discoveryPrefixHint: MQTT discovery topic prefix, default: homeassistant
ha.restarted: The running application was restarted to apply it.
ha.invalidHost: Please enter the MQTT broker host
ha.busy: Another operation is in progress, please retry shortly
ha.discoveryHint: Once enabled and saved, this camera's detection results appear automatically in Home Assistant via MQTT discovery (Settings → Devices & Services → MQTT) — no manual entity setup. Entities update automatically when you switch apps.
ha.rtspHint: The camera publishes a live RTSP stream you can embed in Home Assistant.
ha.gcHint: Add the stream with the built-in Generic Camera integration:
ha.go2rtcHint: Or restream it with go2rtc for low-latency WebRTC playback:

rtsp.title: RTSP live stream
rtsp.subtitle: The camera's raw stream address, usable by anything that speaks RTSP.
rtsp.hint: VLC: Media -> Open Network Stream -> paste the address above. Home Assistant, a VMS and ffmpeg all take the same one.

onvif.title: ONVIF
onvif.subtitle: Make this camera ONVIF-compatible: let video management systems (VMS) discover it and pull the stream, and publish inference results as ONVIF analytics metadata.
onvif.noderedNotice: The device is in Node-RED mode. ONVIF is provided by the Console application — settings saved here take effect after switching back to Console mode.
onvif.serviceHint: Runs the ONVIF device service so a VMS can discover this camera on the network and obtain its RTSP stream URI automatically.
onvif.deviceServiceHint: Paste this device service address into your VMS when adding the camera:
onvif.credentialsHint: Leave the username empty to allow anonymous access.
onvif.passwordUnchanged: Leave empty to keep the current password
onvif.locationHint: Free-form location reported to the VMS, e.g. city/Shenzhen
onvif.metaHint: Publishes inference results using the ONVIF analytics data model, so a VMS or Frigate can consume detections from the stream's metadata track.
onvif.metaExtraTopicHint: The additional ONVIF MQTT topic remains available; existing result publishing is unchanged.
onvif.metaIntervalHint: MQTT metadata interval, 20-60000 ms, default: 200; RTSP metadata follows inference rate
onvif.metaProfileHint: Media profile the metadata is attributed to, default: live0
onvif.metaPrefixHint: Leave empty to use the device serial number
onvif.restarted: The running application was restarted to apply it.
onvif.busy: Another operation is in progress, please retry shortly
onvif.invalidInterval: Interval must be between 20 and 60000 ms
onvif.complianceNote: This device is ONVIF-compatible and implements the ONVIF interfaces described above. It is not an ONVIF-conformant product and carries no ONVIF certification.

blur.title: Privacy blur
blur.subtitle: Mask the subjects the camera detects before the picture is encoded, so faces are already covered in the live stream and in any recording.
blur.noderedNotice: The device is in Node-RED mode. Masking is applied by the Console application — settings saved here take effect after switching back to Console mode.
blur.enabledHint: Covers each detected subject in the picture itself. Nothing unmasked leaves the device.
blur.regionsNote: Up to {{regions}} subjects are masked at the same time. When more are detected, the largest ones in the picture — the closest to the camera — are masked first.

backendHint.pixelate: Blocks take their colour from the picture itself and are composited by the hardware, so this costs almost nothing at runtime.
backendHint.coverex: Solid colour blocks. At most 4 subjects can be masked at once with this style.
backendHint.mosaic: The stock effect of the camera chip. Be aware that it does not pixelate the picture: it draws black-and-white noise over each subject.

blur.blockPxHint: Larger blocks hide more detail. The hardware grid supports these two sizes only.
blur.maxRegionsHint: Between 1 and 8. Extra detections beyond this number are left unmasked.
blur.coverexLimitNotice: Solid colour masking supports at most 4 subjects at once; a higher number will not be honoured with this style.
blur.alphaHint: 255 hides the subject completely; lower values let the picture through in proportion. The debug stream shows the result immediately — judge it against what the site needs.
blur.restarted: The running application was restarted to apply it.
blur.busy: Another operation is in progress, please retry shortly
blur.invalidMaxRegions: The number of subjects must be between 1 and 8

blurDriver.explain: Privacy blur works either way. Without the patched driver the mask is composited by the CPU, which costs about 38 ms per frame; deploying it moves that work into the camera hardware. It replaces two kernel modules and only takes effect after the device is restarted.
blurDriver.unavailableNotPackaged: No patched driver is shipped with this firmware, so there is nothing to deploy.
blurDriver.unavailableVermagic: The packaged driver was built for kernel “{{vermagic}}” but this device runs “{{kernel}}”. Installing it would leave the camera unable to start after the next reboot, so deployment is blocked.
blurDriver.installConfirm: Two kernel modules will be replaced. The factory ones are backed up first and can be restored from this page. The change takes effect only after you restart the device.
blurDriver.restoreConfirm: The backed-up factory modules will be put back and hardware masking acceleration will be lost — the blur keeps working in software, at about 38 ms per frame. The change takes effect only after you restart the device.
blurDriver.doneReboot: Done. Restart the device for the new driver to take effect.
blurDriver.rebootHint: The modules on disk are not the ones the running kernel loaded. Restart the device to apply them.
blurDriver.noBackup: No factory backup exists on this device yet; it is created the first time you deploy.
blurDriver.failed: The driver operation failed; nothing was changed
blurDriver.busy: Another driver operation is in progress, please retry shortly
